key_insight: AdaEvolve replaces fixed, static schedules in LLM-driven evolutionary program search with an adaptive controller that reallocates inference-time compute based on non-stationary search dynamics, substantially reducing wasted evaluations while preserving or improving search outcomes.
problem_solved: Fixed evaluation schedules in LLM-as-mutation evolutionary loops ignore changing population dynamics, causing compute to be wasted on stagnating populations and slowing down program-generation searches.
method: Treat LLMs as semantic mutation operators inside an evolutionary (zeroth-order) search loop during inference-time search.
Continuously monitor search dynamics (e.g., progress, diversity, stagnation) and adapt the allocation of inference/evaluation budget across populations.
Use an adaptive scheduling policy to prioritize promising subpopulations and throttle or reallocate resources away from stagnating ones.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, AdaEvolve means more cost-efficient program synthesis and optimization using LLMs—reducing unnecessary compute and accelerating search without changing the underlying model. It enables scalable, practical deployment of LLM-driven search in resource-constrained settings.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the evolutionary loop showing LLM as mutation operator and an adaptive scheduler that monitors populations and reallocates compute.

Line plot illustrating non-stationary search dynamics (progress/diversity over time) with adaptive intervention points marked.
Icon set: LLM model, clock/compute budget, population clusters, and a reallocation arrow to convey adaptive resource shifting.
paper_title: AdaEvolve: Adaptive LLM Driven Zeroth-Order Optimization
paper_authors: Mert Cemri, Shubham Agrawal, Akshat Gupta, Shu Liu, Audrey Cheng
